pr_body:
Add three new limits to the scrape configuration to provide some
mechanism to defend against unbound number of labels and excessive
label lengths. If any of these limits are broken by a sample from a
scrape, the whole scrape will fail. For all of these configuration
options, a zero value means no limit.

The `label_limit` configuration will provide a mechanism to bound the
number of labels per-scrape of a certain sample to a user defined limit.
This limit will be tested against the sample labels plus the discovery
labels.

The `label_name_length_limit` and `label_value_length_limit` will
prevent having labels of excessive lengths. These limits will
also make the scrape fail if any sample has a label name/value length
that exceed the predefined limits.

Fixes #8291
pr_comments:
Thank you for this pull request, it looks great.

The limits should apply to `__name__`.

We should also truncate the names/values (e.g. to 50 chars) in the errors I think. When there are to many labels we could also only display the `__name__ label`.

Thank you for the review @roidelapluie, I'll update the PR to include your suggestions.

> We should also truncate the names/values (e.g. to 50 chars) in the errors I think.

Instead of truncating which might be a bit confusing to users, what do you think about only displaying `__name__` and the problematic label in the error?
If the issue is the label name too long (and it could be very very long) we should truncate it in the error message.

issue_context.title: Add more scrape limits
issue_context.body:
As per the last dev summit:

We want to implement the easy, configurable defenses, like label name/value length and number of scraped labels. We will fail the scrape when hit. We will provide counters to make this easy for users.

The above will be configurable during runtime.

cc @lilic
comments: Looking forward to this feature! Would be interesting in tackling this, but most likely cannot get to it until next year, is that still okay? Thanks!
Yes, totally okay, I will assign to you. End of the year is always a quiet period.

So @roidelapluie before I start the work, to understand correctly we want to add the following config fields:
- limit for the number of scraped labels -> `LabelLimit`
- limit for the length of label name -> `LabelNameLenghtLimit`
- limit for the length of value name -> `LabelValueLenghtLimit`

Let me know if I missed any here, and if you have any better naming suggestions for the fields to be more self-descriptive, thanks!

>The above will be configurable during runtime.

Does this mean that, the values can be increased, decreased at runtime. Would there be any side effects especially when values are decreased?

> > The above will be configurable during runtime.
> 
> Does this mean that, the values can be increased, decreased at runtime. Would there be any side effects especially when values are decreased?

When values are changed we would invalidate scrape cache. That should not be visible to users.

Sadly I never got the time to work on this, due to other higher priority tasks. Now since leaving the team, I have handed the task over to @dgrisonnet. 

But thank you @roidelapluie for pinging me on it! 🙇‍♀️
Happy to take over @lilic's work on this feature :slightly_smiling_face:

Nice, some follow up question regarding:

> limit for the number of scraped labels -> LabelLimit

Do we mean per single metrics or per job or overall in Prometheus?
this is a scrape job setting that applies to any metric post relabelling

review_comments: Maybe stupid question, but can we fail to scrape the problematic series instead of the whole target? 🤔

No we can not. There would be multiple issues with failing only some labels.
It would be inconsistent with all the scrape limits we have.

Also, we do not support half-ingested scrapes and should not. It would lead to incomplete query results at the end for the user.
That'd be very difficult for users to deal with correctly, plus would violate the OpenMetrics spec. See https://www.robustperception.io/remote-read-and-partial-failures for the reasoning.
